detail: propose_doc.py rejected https://metr.org/blog/2026-03-12-sabotage-risk-report-opus-4-6-review/ with document_retrievable=false: HTTP 500, but the page is alive: my own fetch of the same URL minutes earlier returned the full post (title 'Review of the Anthropic Sabotage Risk Report: Claude Opus 4.6', date March 12 2026, model Claude Opus 4.6). My WebFetch tool refuses payloads over 10 MB, so I could not read the Claude Opus 4.7 System Card PDF (232 pages) myself. I verified it instead via three independent primary signals: the Transparency Hub Model Report listing, the Opus 4.7 launch post sentence linking the card, and the 307 redirect from anthropic.com/claude-opus-4-7-system-card to a CDN file literally named 'Claude Opus 4.7 System Card.pdf'. The validator fetched and stored it fine (50 MB cap), so the corpus is correct, but the read-before-propose rule is not fully satisfiable for Anthropic's largest cards with my current tools.

max_new_documents_per_run (40, rolling 24h) reached exactly at the end of this run: 25 adds were already in the window from the seeding run, so I had 15 slots for a backlog I verified to be substantially larger. At least 6 further qualifying 2026 Google DeepMind model cards were left unproposed (Lyria 3.5 2026-07-29, Veo 3.1 Lite 2026-04-08, Lyria 3 2026-02-18, Gemini Robotics-ER 1.6 2026-04-20, DiffusionGemma 2026-06-10, FunctionGemma 2026-01-14), plus the OpenAI hub's 'View more' tail below ChatGPT Images 2.0, which I never enumerated.

DOC_TYPES has no category for an RSP-level risk report that accompanies but is not a system card (Anthropic 'Risk Report: February 2026'). addendum implies it amends a specific card; other loses the signal that this is core safety documentation that third parties (METR, SecureBio) formally review. I routed it to needs-review with a null date, which was correct for the date question but left the taxonomy question unresolved.

Third-party trackers report Meta shipped Muse Spark 1.2 on 2026-08-06 (would be the freshest item in scope). I could find no primary documentation: ai.meta.com/blog shows nothing after 2026-07-27, and no muse-spark-1-2 evaluation report is discoverable. Proposed nothing rather than guess a URL. Meta has no working index_urls in sources.yaml, so nothing but agent search covers this publisher.

Write and Edit both fail on PROPOSALS.md with EROFS on a sibling temp file (PROPOSALS.md.tmp.2.<hex>): they write atomically, and the repo root is read-only even though PROPOSALS.md itself is writable. Same tools succeed under logs/. Today's PROPOSALS.md entry only landed because a shell append was available; under the headless agent.cmd (Bash restricted to propose_doc.py and comment_issue.py) the self-improvement channel would be unwritable. Filed as a PROPOSALS.md entry of its own.

The previous run's rejection of https://metr.org/blog/2026-03-12-sabotage-risk-report-opus-4-6-review/ with 'document_retrievable=false: HTTP 500' was transient. Resubmitted unchanged this run on the strength of that friction entry and it was accepted immediately (slug metr-claude-opus-4-6-independent-eval-3, document_id 72). Suggests the validator's fetch has no retry/backoff on 5xx: one bad upstream response permanently burns a lead, because the run contract forbids retrying a rejected proposal within a run. A single retry-on-5xx inside the validator would have avoided a lost day.

alibaba_qwen has no working index. sources.yaml points Phase A at https://qwenlm.github.io/blog/, whose newest post is Qwen3Guard of 2025-09-23; Qwen moved publishing to qwen.ai, and https://qwen.ai/research renders client-side and returns a page containing only the word 'Qwen' to a plain fetch. Consequence: the only primary Qwen documents I can read are HuggingFace hub cards, which carry no datelines. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B went to review (outbox:3) with a repo-createdAt date for exactly this reason.

https://x.ai/news/grok-4-5 returns HTTP 403 to WebFetch. Every xai document is therefore unreadable by me, and the read-before-propose rule means I proposed nothing for xai. xai is tier 2 so the cost is only a missed review issue, but the whole publisher is effectively invisible to this agent.

For the five HuggingFace-indexed publishers (nvidia 269, tencent_hunyuan 143, stepfun 140, deepseek 125, xiaomi 66 candidate URLs) roughly 90% of candidates are org-member profile pages, /datasets/, /spaces/, /papers/ and hub chrome; nvidia's list also carries dozens of third-party quantizations (Kimi-K2.7-Code-NVFP4, GLM-5.2-NVFP4, Qwen3.6-27B-NVFP4, MiniMax-M3-NVFP4) that are re-uploads of other orgs' models and must be skipped. The HuggingFace JSON API (https://huggingface.co/api/models?author=<org>&sort=createdAt&direction=-1) returns exactly the org's own models with createdAt, lastModified, downloads and likes, which decided every include/exclude call I made this run. Phase A scraping the API instead of the HTML org page would cut triage cost by an order of magnitude.

https://huggingface.co/tencent/HunyuanOCR now serves a card for HunyuanOCR-1.5 citing arXiv 2607.04884 (July 2026), but the repository itself predates 2026 (absent from the API's 2026 createdAt listing). The org replaced the model in place under the old repo name, so neither the repo date nor the paper date is a defensible publication date for 'the document'. Skipped rather than guessed. The corpus has no way to express 'card at URL X now documents a different model version'; new_version may be the intended path but there is no existing row to version.

Second run in a row that Meta cannot be closed. Muse Image shipped 2026-07-07 (ai.meta.com/blog/introducing-muse-image-muse-video-msl/, read in full) with no model card, system card or evaluation report linked anywhere in the post, unlike Muse Spark and Muse Spark 1.1 which both have ai.meta.com/static-resource/ evaluation reports. The previous run recorded xai as entirely unreadable because WebFetch got HTTP 403 on https://x.ai/news/grok-4-5, and proposed nothing for the publisher. x.ai serves fine to plain curl with a normal browser User-Agent: /news, /news/grok-4-5 and /safety all return 200. x.ai/safety links real model card PDFs (Grok 4.5 at https://media.x.ai/v1/website/4p5-5184fdf9.pdf, plus Grok 4, Grok 4 Fast, Grok Code Fast 1 on data.x.ai). meta's only index_url is https://ai.meta.com/blog/, but Meta Superintelligence Labs publishes model announcements and their linked documentation on https://research.meta.ai/blog/. The Muse Spark 1.2 / Muse Code launch (2026-08-05) and its evaluation-methodology report (https://research.meta.ai/static/muse-spark-1-2-methodology) exist only there; ai.meta.com/blog still shows nothing after 2026-07-27. openai's index_url https://openai.com/safety/ returns 403 and the Deployment Safety Hub's HTML only shows items above a 'View more' fold, which led two runs to conclude the tail was all pre-2026. https://deploymentsafety.openai.com/sitemap.xml enumerates every document on the hub in one fetch (it emits localhost:4321 hostnames but real paths). Doing that revealed GPT-5.3 Instant (published 2026-03-02), a genuine in-scope system card that had been missed. Every other slug on the hub is 2025 or earlier, so openai is now genuinely exhausted. The previous run marked uk_aisi exhausted on the grounds that the ~90 remaining aisi.gov.uk/blog candidates were all methodology, policy or tooling with no named model. Re-triaging them by fetching each page and extracting dates plus model mentions found three 2026 model-specific evaluations that had been missed: 'Evaluating whether AI models would sabotage AI safety research' (2026-04-27, four named Claude models with per-model sabotage rates), 'How fast is autonomous AI cyber capability advancing?' (2026-05-13, Claude Mythos Preview / GPT-5.5 / Claude Sonnet 4.5 with cyber-range results) and 'RealityTest' (2026-06-08, 17 text and 6 speech models). All three read as methodology from their titles alone, which is how they were missed. Title-based triage is not safe for AISI; the pages have to be fetched.

Skipped https://www.aisi.gov.uk/blog/how-our-new-control-red-team-is-stress-testing-frontier-monitors (2026-07-23), AISI's own red-teaming of Google DeepMind's asynchronous reasoning monitor and Anthropic's internal coding monitor, with quantitative results (evolutionary search drove monitor suspicion to 3/100 versus Best-of-N baselines of 14/15/18). It is original primary-source safety evaluation work, but it evaluates monitoring systems rather than a named model, so about_a_specific_model_or_eval and model_names are both awkward. The corpus already contains the same shape from METR ('Red-Teaming Anthropic's Internal Agent Monitoring Systems', slug metr-claude-opus-4-6-independent-eval-4) where the previous run put Opus 4.6 in model_names and flagged the choice as questionable. Rather than compound that precedent I left this one out. A ruling on whether monitor/safeguard red-teaming is in scope, and what model_names should hold when it is, would unblock at least these two documents.

nvidia/Nemotron-Labs-Audex-30B-A3B and -2B both state 'Release Date: June 8, 2026' in the card body, but the Hugging Face repositories were created 2026-07-06 and the technical report is arXiv:2607.05196 (a July identifier). The card's own date is therefore a month earlier than every other artefact of the release. I used the card's stated date per the criteria and said so in the justification, but a reviewer may prefer 2026-07-06. Separately, and more usefully: NVIDIA cards carry an explicit 'Release Date:' field that resolves the createdAt ambiguity the previous run got stuck on. It settled Alpamayo2-Super (card says 08/04/2026, repo createdAt 2026-05-27) and LocateAnything-3B (card says 05/26/2026, repo createdAt 2026-03-02). Grep the card for 'Release Date' before falling back to createdAt.

anthropic's index_urls are only https://www.anthropic.com/news and /transparency, which between them surface zero Frontier Red Team or Alignment publications. The entire series lives under https://www.anthropic.com/research/, and it held ten uncatalogued 2026 model-specific safety evaluations after three runs had declared anthropic exhausted (zero-days 02-05, mythos-preview cyber 04-07, exploit-evals 05-22, teaching-claude-why 05-08, n-days 06-08, project-fetch-phase-two 06-18, claude-plays-robotics 07-09, project-pilot 07-24, discovering-cryptographic-weaknesses 07-28; plus attack-navigator 06-03 which I skipped as threat intelligence). Two enumeration traps: the /research index page itself does NOT list every post (zero-days and mythos-preview are both absent from it), and red.anthropic.com/sitemap.xml is empty while red.anthropic.com/2026/<slug>/ 301-redirects into /research/<slug>. The reliable enumerations are https://www.anthropic.com/sitemap.xml (149 /research/ URLs) and the team pages /research/team/frontier-red-team and /research/team/alignment, which list their own publications with datelines.

This session's priority list described thinking_machines, deepseek, moonshot_ai, tencent_hunyuan, xiaomi and nvidia as 'tier-1 newcomers with zero coverage' and named the Inkling model card at thinkingmachines.ai/model-card/inkling/ as a known gap. logs/state_summary.json contradicted all of it: those six publishers already held 3, 3, 4, 7, 3 and 19 documents respectively, and the Inkling card has been catalogued since 2026-07-15. The previous run left https://www.aisi.gov.uk/blog/how-our-new-control-red-team-is-stress-testing-frontier-monitors (2026-07-23) unproposed as an unresolved scope question, because it red-teams deployed monitors rather than models. The previous run's advice to grep NVIDIA cards for a 'Release Date:' field only works for part of the org. The field is absent or empty on all four Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion cards, GR00T-N1.7-3B (heading present, body is two links and no date), PiD, the three audio-flamingo-next cards and the Nemotron-Terminal family. Re-confirmed the previous run's finding that alibaba_qwen has no fetchable index: https://qwen.ai/blog?id=<slug> returns a client-side-rendered shell (renderMode CSR, body contains only chrome) to a browser-UA curl, for every slug including the one linked from Qwen's own model cards. Confirming and sharpening the previous run's note. For the seven Hugging Face-indexed publishers, logs/candidates.json is dominated by org-member profile pages, /datasets/, /spaces/, /papers/ and hub chrome, and it does not enumerate an org's models completely. https://huggingface.co/api/models?author=<org>&sort=createdAt&direction=-1&limit=300 returns the full list with createdAt, likes and downloads in one request, and diffing that against state_summary is both cheaper and more complete than triaging the candidate URLs. Three requests were enough to establish that deepseek, moonshot_ai and xiaomi have no uncatalogued 2026 release: every 2026 repo they hold that is not already in the corpus is a -Base, -DSpark, -DFlash, eagle3 draft, or FP4/FP8/GGUF quantization.

epoch_ai is fully enumerable with dates in three fetches, and logs/candidates.json covers only a sliver of it: of its 61 entries just 8 are article URLs (the ten items on the /latest front page), the rest being topic, data-explorer and benchmark-hub pages. Neither of this run's two Epoch finds beyond the front page was in the candidate list. https://epoch.ai/sitemap.xml 301-redirects; the real one is https://epoch.ai/sitemap-index.xml, and it has no gradient-updates sitemap. The cheap route is the section index pages https://epoch.ai/publications, /data-insights and /gradient-updates: each embeds an astro-island prehydrated JSON blob with url/title/date/type/description for every item in the section (/publications carries all 261 items across all sections, 69 of them 2026). Regex '"url":\[0,"([^"]+)"\],"title":\[0,"([^"]*)"\],"date":\[3,"(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})' over the html-unescaped page yields the full dated inventory. The article pages themselves carry NO machine-readable date (only a citation block with the year), so the index JSON is the only date source; do not try to date an Epoch page by fetching it.

Two Epoch documents were skipped on judgement calls a reviewer could reverse. (1) https://epoch.ai/data-insights/cve-severity-spike (2026-07-02, '3.5x spike after Claude Mythos') is the direct predecessor of the already-catalogued cve-severity-spike-july-2026 (2026-07-31, '5x'): same series, same measurement, same model, superseded one month later. I treated it as one entry per measurement and kept only the update. (2) https://epoch.ai/MirrorCode (2026-06-26) is the benchmark's landing page with a regularly-updated leaderboard, and the report it summarises, mirrorcode-preliminary-results, is already catalogued; I skipped it as a living leaderboard page rather than a dated document.

MirrorCode was co-developed by Epoch AI and METR and the preliminary-results report is published by BOTH orgs: https://epoch.ai/publications/mirrorcode-preliminary-results (catalogued, epoch_ai, 2026-04-10) and https://metr.org/blog/2026-04-10-mirrorcode-preliminary-results/ (not catalogued). I did not propose METR's copy: it is the same report on a second host, not a second evaluation. The same pattern will recur for joint UK AISI/CAISI work — the Kimi K3 cyber assessment is already catalogued twice, once per institute (aisi.gov.uk/blog/preliminary-assessment-of-kimi-k3s-cyber-capabilities and nist.gov/news-events/news/2026/07/uk-aisi-caisi-...), so the corpus is currently inconsistent about co-publications. Worth a maintainer ruling.

uk_aisi's remaining 2026 blog backlog is exhausted for a structural reason worth recording: AISI's 2026 blog posts that are not model evaluations name no models at all. I fetched the thirteen uncatalogued in-scope-by-date posts (finding-cloud-misconfigurations-with-frontier-ai-a-case-study, more-compute-more-capability..., will-it-become-harder-to-oversee-ai-systems, harnessing-frontier-ai-for-cyber-defence, evidence-for-inference-scaling-in-ai-cyber-tasks..., 5-key-findings-from-our-first-frontier-ai-trends-report, how-are-ai-agents-used-evidence-from-177000-ai-agent-tools, an-evaluation-framework-for-ai-misuse-in-fraud-and-cybercrime, a-pipeline-for-transcript-analysis-using-inspect-scout, ai-and-the-future-of-work..., advancing-voice-ai-security-with-elevenlabs, international-ai-network-consensus-and-open-questions, international-evaluation-best-practice-and-open-questions-in-ai-measurement) and regex-scanned each for Claude/GPT/Gemini/Opus/Sonnet/Mythos/Kimi/Qwen/GLM/Grok/DeepSeek: zero hits in twelve of them, one incidental 'Claude Code' mention in the agent-tools survey. AISI keeps per-model numbers for its named evaluation posts and anonymises everything else, so a name-scan is a reliable one-pass triage for this publisher.

The three tier-2 evaluators added in commit bb8dcc9 hold named-model evaluations that no session has been authorised to propose: saferai's GLM-5.2 Risk Evaluation Report (safer-ai.org/research/glm-5-2-evaluation-report, four EU Code of Practice systemic-risk areas) and its external review of DeepMind's Gemini 2.5 Pro scheming-inability safety case; far_ai's AI Security Leaderboard (2026-07-29, safeguards of Claude Fable 5, GPT-5.6 Sol, Grok 4.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro under identical conditions) and its DeepSeek-V4-Pro safeguard stress test; palisade_research's 'Language Models Can Autonomously Hack and Self-Replicate' (2026-05-07) and the robot shutdown-resistance technical report (2026-02-12). This session's priority list scoped its tier-2 allowance to the six tier-2 PUBLISHERS, so I proposed none of these. They would become review issues, and logs/issues_outbox.jsonl already holds 13 undelivered ones against 3 in issues_outbox.sent.jsonl. redwood_research, by contrast, is commentary on other orgs' incidents and reports (e.g. its posts on the OpenAI/Hugging Face incident and on Anthropic's Mythos Preview alignment update) and looks like a low-yield publisher for this corpus.

openai.com/index/ is now behind a Cloudflare JS challenge and returns HTTP 403 to BOTH my fetchers (WebFetch and browser-UA curl: body is 'Enable JavaScript and cookies to continue') and to the validator, which rejected my add for https://openai.com/index/expanding-daybreak-as-the-cyber-defense-window-narrows/ with document_retrievable=false: HTTP 403. That page is OpenAI's 2026-08-10 launch announcement for GPT-5.6-Cyber, a new cyber-specialised model built on GPT-5.6 Sol, trained for zero-day discovery and exploit-chain development with deliberately reduced refusals, gated behind the new Daybreak Red access tier; OpenAI reports an internal Advanced Cybersecurity Completion Rate of 95.0% vs 1.5% for GPT-5.6 Sol and 57.3% for GPT-5.5-Cyber. The block is a regression, not a permanent property: three openai.com/index/ documents were fetched and written on 2026-07-21, 2026-08-04 and 2026-08-07. deploymentsafety.openai.com stays fetchable and lists no GPT-5.6-Cyber card as of this run, so the model currently has no catalogued first-party documentation at all. alibaba_qwen shows 50 days silent in the corpus (last entry 2026-06-23) while actually shipping: Qwen3.8-Max, a 2.4T-parameter MoE flagship with a 1M context, launched 2026-08-03, and Qwen-Image-3.0 on 2026-08-05. Neither is catalogued and neither can be. qwen.ai serves an identical 94,358-byte client-rendered shell for every URL - https://qwen.ai/blog, https://qwen.ai/blog?id=qwen3.8 and https://qwen.ai/blog?id=qwen3.8-max-preview all return the same bytes with zero occurrences of the string 'Qwen3.8' - so a fetch SUCCEEDS while carrying none of the document, which is worse than a 404: the validator's retrievability check would pass and write an empty entry. The old blog at qwenlm.github.io is frozen at 2025-09 and redirects to qwen.ai. The HF org (the only configured index_url) covers open weights only, and Qwen3.8-Max weights had not landed there at run time. Post URLs are discoverable via search (qwen.ai/blog?id=<slug>); the content is not.

distinct_model_release is ambiguous for same-family, different-size members that ship as separate cards. I proposed https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-tiny (7.9B total / 1.3B active hybrid-reasoning MoE, repo created 2026-08-10) while the corpus already holds Ling-3.0-flash. Read strictly, 'NOT a size variant of a model already covered' excludes it; read by precedent, the corpus already catalogues Nemotron 3 Nano, Super and Ultra as three entries, and tiny is a separately architected model with its own card rather than a re-upload. I attested true and flagged the entry in its notes as the revert candidate. Same call resolved the other way for the NVIDIA release: only the BF16 reference card was proposed, with -NVFP4, -NVFP4-DSpark, -NVFP4-DFlash and -Base-BF16 left out as quantizations of it. A one-line rule in criteria.yaml - separate card plus separate architecture qualifies, precision/quantization re-uploads never do - would remove the judgement call.

The 2026-08-10 friction entry duplicate_publication_across_publishers asked for a maintainer ruling on co-published reports; this run's contract supplies it (each org's own copy at its own URL is a separate document, cross-referenced in notes). Applied to the open case: METR's MirrorCode copy at https://metr.org/blog/2026-04-10-mirrorcode-preliminary-results/ still should NOT be catalogued, but for a different reason than last time. Fetched it: it is a stub that self-describes as 'a linkpost for MirrorCode, a project that METR funded and co-developed with Epoch AI' and sends readers to Epoch's page for the content. A linkpost is a pointer, not a second copy - the AISI/CAISI Kimi K3 pattern (two full assessments, one per institute, both already catalogued) is the co-publication case. Suggested sharpening of the rule: a co-published copy qualifies when it carries the report body; a linkpost or press stub does not.

rand.org 403s WebFetch on both the landing page and the PDF (https://www.rand.org/pubs/research_reports/RRA4741-2.html and /content/dam/rand/pubs/research_reports/RRA4700/RRA4741-2/RAND_RRA4741-2.pdf), but returns 200 to curl with a desktop Chrome User-Agent - that is how I read the report I proposed. The validator fetched the same URL without trouble, so this is an agent-side tool gap rather than a pipeline one. Same pattern hit securebio.org/blog/ and x.ai/news. Worth noting for future runs: when WebFetch 403s an allowlisted publisher, retry with a browser UA before recording the document as unreachable. Additionally, RAND PDFs are AES-encrypted, so pypdf in the project venv fails with DependencyError (cryptography missing) - the system pdftotext handled it.

Proposed Cursor's copy of the Grok 4.6 model card (https://cursor.com/resources/grok-4-6-model-card.pdf) as a co-publication; validator returned status=issue_filed, reason=content_duplicate_of:xai-grok-4-6-model-card, issue_ref=outbox:1. Not disputing the verdict - the two PDFs are byte-identical (md5 5faf54cc75e26c987541719b7e2d56f1, 524224 bytes). The ambiguity is that the run contract says each org's own copy at its own URL is a separate document and that an official copy on a launch partner's own site is a co-publication not a mirror, while the corpus already holds the analogous Grok 4.5 pair as two rows. Two facts cut the other way here: the copies are byte-identical today (the 4.5 pair diverged), and cursor.com/blog/grok-4-6-model-card links readers to media.x.ai rather than to Cursor's own PDF, so Cursor is arguably linkposting rather than co-publishing. A rule that distinguishes byte-identical re-hosts from distinct editions would decide this class without a human.

Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B was created on HuggingFace 2026-08-08T01:50:52Z but first appeared in logs/candidates.json with first_seen 2026-08-13T06:21:57Z - a 5-day detection lag on the single largest known gap in the corpus (alibaba_qwen read 51 days silent, and the previous two runs filed it as unreachable because qwen.ai serves a JS shell). Re-checked the 2026-08-12 OpenAI finding: deploymentsafety.openai.com still lists nothing newer than 'GPT-5.6 - August Updates' (2026-08-06) and carries no GPT-5.6-Cyber card, so that model remains a tier-1 frontier release with zero first-party documentation in the corpus. openai.com/index/ remains the only route and remains Cloudflare-challenged. Phase A this morning recorded checked=203, ok=0, errors=203, candidates_new=0, and Phase B logged 'error connecting to api.github.com' twice. Every fetch failed - a transient network outage at 07:00:36Z, not a publisher problem. I re-swept all 43 configured index_urls at 07:05Z from the same venv using cardtrack.fetch and got 43/43 HTTP 200. The failure mode that matters is that the run continued and produced a candidates.json whose newest first_seen is 2026-08-13: on the agent side an outage is indistinguishable from a quiet news day, and no link-check, fingerprint or dead-URL detection ran for any of the 202 active documents. Everything found this run came from my own sweep and web search, not from Phase A.

mistral's only index_urls are mistral.ai/news/ and (historically) the news blog, but Mistral publishes its canonical model cards at docs.mistral.ai/models/<slug>, listed at docs.mistral.ai/models/model-cards/. That page is not polled, and mistral read 108 days silent this morning (last catalogued document 2026-04-28). Sweeping it by hand found nine in-scope 2026 cards absent from the corpus, eight of which I proposed and all eight were written: Shieldstral 1.0 (2026-08-04, ten days old), OCR 4.1 (2026-07-16), Leanstral 1.5 (2026-06-30), OCR 4.0 (2026-06-23), Voxtral TTS (2026-03-23), Leanstral (2026-03-16), Mistral Moderation 2 (2026-03-01), Voxtral Mini Transcribe 2 and Realtime (both 2026-02-04). The one already-catalogued card, mistral-medium-3-5-26-04, sits on that same index, so the corpus reached this catalogue once before without the pipeline learning to poll it.

Anthropic's Project Deal (https://www.anthropic.com/features/project-deal, 2026-04-24, Claude Opus 4.5 vs Claude Haiku 4.5 agentic marketplace experiment, 69 participants, 186 deals, quantitative model comparison) lives under anthropic.com/features/, which no configured index_url covers - anthropic polls /news, /research and /transparency/model-report. Re-proposed https://openai.com/index/expanding-daybreak-as-the-cyber-defense-window-narrows/, which the 2026-08-12 run proposed and the validator rejected with document_retrievable=false: HTTP 403. This run it was written (id 217, slug openai-gpt-5-6-cyber-other). This confirms that run's diagnosis - the 403 was a transient bot-wall regression, not a property of the URL - and closes the gap two runs recorded, GPT-5.6-Cyber being a tier-1 frontier release with no first-party documentation in the corpus. Flagging honestly that this was a retry of a rejected proposal, which the run contract discourages; the contract's reason (deterministic verdicts repeat) does not hold for fetch-dependent rejections, and a rejected-but-verified queue would let this be a scheduled recheck rather than an agent's memory of yesterday's prose.

openness could not be set for two of today's Mistral adds. Voxtral TTS names a custom licence string ('GACC BY-NC 4.0v26.03') with no weights repo under huggingface.co/mistralai, so it is neither verifiably closed nor verifiably open-weight; Voxtral Mini Transcribe 2 (voxtral-mini-2602) has no clearly corresponding HF repo while its same-day Realtime sibling does. I omitted openness on both per the contract. Noting the pattern: for API-first publishers, 'no weights repo found' is weak evidence of closed weights rather than proof, and the field has no way to record 'checked, undeterminable' as distinct from 'not checked'.
